Nvidia Soared 35% on Jensen Huang's Return. Is It Too Late to Buy?

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (632 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that if you've been following the fast-moving Jensen Huang drama at Nvidia (NVDA +31.48%), you probably have a severe case of whiplash this morning.
  • In response, Nvidia's shares jumped as much as 35% intraday after falling 47.5% from their early October highs.
  • Recent findings suggest that given the size of the jump, is it too late to buy Nvidia stock?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By John Bromels – Nov 23, 2026 at 3:31PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

It has been revealed that if you've been following the fast-moving Jensen Huang drama at Nvidia (NVDA +31.48%), you probably have a severe case of whiplash this morning. Nvidia declared today that its board unanimously voted to reinstate the former CEO less than two weeks after his resignation.

In response, Nvidia's shares jumped as much as 35% intraday after falling 47.5% from their early October highs.

Recent findings suggest that given the size of the jump, is it too late to buy Nvidia stock? I don't think so. Here's why.

Jensen Huang. Image source: Nvidia.

The Jensen Huang soap opera -- which includes reports of foreign spies, lurid affairs, and shocking reversals of fortune -- is hard to look away from. Indeed, it's easily the most exciting drama to hit the stock market in years. But it's the kind of drama that doesn't tend to impact long-term results.

No, it's never a good thing when your CEO's name is plastered all over the news as having had an affair with a potential foreign spy, but unless there are ongoing national security implications for the manufacturer, the business should keep chugging along regardless.

Recent findings suggest that and chug along it has. Nvidia's Q3 revenue hit $115.8 billion, up 103% year over year (YOY), and up 20% from the prior quarter. Meanwhile, data center revenue totaled $107.6 billion, up 110% year over year. Gross margins stayed close to 75%. Net income more than doubled YOY to $65.3 billion, while management guided for about $130 billion in Q4 revenue (which would be a 91% year-over-year increase).

That Q4 projection, it's worth noting, was made by CFO Colette Kress after Huang's resignation and prior to his reinstatement. It seems unlikely that Huang's return would result in lower projections. If anything, the sense that Nvidia has put its drama behind it might only improve its outlook.

But is the drama actually in Nvidia's rearview mirror?

Various figures within the Trump administration, including the president himself, publicly backed Huang prior to today's surprise reinstatement.

Afterward, Trump took credit for the reinstatement, telling CNBC that he had spoken to Nvidia's board and given them "assurances at least with everything we know, and we know a lot," reiterating that, in his view, Huang "did nothing wrong.".

If Nvidia's board was concerned that national security risks or consequences tied to Huang's personal behavior or business activities could blow back on the tech giant as a whole, it's unlikely they would have unanimously approved his return.

Last week, the board created a national security and export control oversight committee, with an independent investigation ongoing, so investors can't quite regard the matter as fully closed.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

Nvidia's growth comes from a product lineup, supply chain, and customer relationships built by thousands of people over many years. There was never a good reason to expect that growth to flag without Huang aboard. Still, his return should soothe a nervous market.

Even after the 35% post-reinstatement surge, Nvidia's stock is still down about 11% for the year, despite quarter after quarter of strong results. That gap suggests the market has been pricing in more worry than the fundamentals warrant. In my view, there's still plenty of room for shares to run.

I upgraded to an Apple Watch Series 12 this fall (now $329 on Amazon), and there are four main features that make me especially glad I did.

The Apple Watch was overdue for a chip upgrade, with Apple skipping any changes last year and not having any true performance upgrades since the S9.

I’m happy to report that the new S11 chip appears much faster and more capable than its predecessor, the S10.

Everyday tasks on Apple Watch Series 12 just feel fast. And Siri AI, a tentpole addition in watchOS 27, very much feels made for this latest hardware. Siri was sluggish on older hardware in my testing, but it performs much more like I’d hoped on Series 12.

The upcoming Health Sensing System makes Apple Watch Series 12 better at tracking key metrics like heart rate and steps. But this isn’t a case where accuracy is the only improvement.

Because of the newly introduced health sensors, Series 12 offers three complications not available before:.

The complications let you see up-to-date readings on your current heart rate, step count, and readiness score right from your watch face. These are very welcome additions that meaningfully improve the Apple Watch’s health and wellness feature set.

I’ve been using the watchOS 27.3 beta, which adds a latest Siri Recap feature for Series 12 models that I really love.

Siri Recap ambiently takes notes on your conversations throughout your day and creates high-level Apple Intelligence–generated summaries that you can use later to jog your memory, so you can stay present in the moment.

In a recent development, most of what Siri documents, I’ll never need to reference and it gets deleted automatically. But for those times I have trouble remembering a key piece of information, I’ve found Siri Recap a very convenient addition.

Apple Watch Series 12 offers largely the same battery life as Series 11, though it will last 25% longer for outdoor workouts.

More battery is always nice, but I’m especially a fan of the faster charging available on Series 12. Here’s how it stacks up to Series 11:.

I wear my Apple Watch to bed and generally try to top it off promptly in the evening, but I’m not always great at giving it much time on the charger. With faster charging support on Series 12, my poor planning isn’t a problem.

Apple Watch Series 12 is now only $329 on Amazon, down from $399.

Have you upgraded to Apple Watch Series 12? Why or why not? Let us know in the comments.

According to recent reports, I'm Tom's Guide's resident coffee expert, and I've tested well over 50 coffee makers. Everything from iconic Breville machines like the Bambino Plus and Oracle Dual Boiler to the De'Longhi PrimaDonna Aromatic to the Lelit Mara X3 to the Nespresso Vertuo Up — I've done 'em all. You name it, I've tested it.

So I'm uniquely positioned to find all the best espresso machine deals this Black Friday and help you spend your money wisely. Bar two, every machine on here I've either tested or have in the pipeline. (And the two I haven't tested are Brevilles — my favorite consumer espresso machine brand).

According to recent reports, I've tested well over 50 coffee makers, I direct The Coffee Lab, and I'm a self-professed coffee snob. As Tom's Guide's resident coffee expert, I'm here to help you choose the perfect espresso machine this Black Friday.

The most affordable option on this list, the BELLA Jolt is also the smallest. At under 6 inches wide and 11 inches tall, it's ideal for compact kitchens. I've not tested this one completely — but I've got the machine and it's in the pipeline! If you're a coffee newbie, I'd recommend grabbing the Jolt on sale.

Sources indicate that the Lavazza Tabli is one of the most exciting espresso machines of 2026, and maybe even all time. This machine uses 100% pure coffee pods — zero plastic or metal, unlike Keurig and Nespresso. The espresso genuinely tastes delicious, and it's just as easy to use as any other pod machine. I refuse to shut up about the Tabli. It's just too good.

According to recent reports, for the home baristas who want hot coffee in seconds, a Nespresso machine is the best bet. This Vertuo Pop+ combines an Instagrammable appearance with Nespresso's signature ease of use to make espresso in no time. The Vertuo line offers a wider range of coffee flavors, too, and can even make a full mug without needing to top it up.

The Casabrews CM5418 went a little viral on TikTok last year for being pretty and extremely cheap. Even though it takes a little while to switch between espresso and steam and requires some boiler purging, at this price point, you're not going to get much better. It looks cute and is easy to use — as long as you purge that boiler!

Sources indicate that the De'Longhi Classic is a great first espresso machine. This model is super easy to use and forgiving for newbies (especially if you're using pre-ground coffee). While the steam wand only really makes foam rather than microfoam, this is fine if you're a total newbie or you're a cappuccino addict.

Industry observers note that for coffee lovers both short on time and money, a Nespresso machine is a great option. The Nespresso Vertuo Up uses patented "Vertuo" pods (these come in a wider range of flavors than the original line) and makes hot coffee at the press of a button. The newly introduced Up even makes iced drinks, perfect for summer.

The Ninja Luxe Cafe Mini is the perfect first espresso machine. Thanks to its small footprint (my sister has this machine and it fits into her tiny kitchen perfectly) and built-in grinder, it minimizes clutter and cleanup. I tested the Plus version of this machine earlier this year and was blown away by its ease of use and compact style — the only difference is the Plus has automated milk frothing.

Recent findings suggest that the Creatista Plus is one of the only Nespresso machines with a built-in barista-style steam wand. This model uses Nespresso pods for the coffee and its very own steam wand for the milk — just like a "real" espresso machine. Usually espresso-machine-priced at $600, it's now $390.

It has been revealed that the De'Longhi La Specialista Arte Evo is the best-value bean-to-cup on this list. While it lacks the PID controller present on the Breville Barista Express, the powerful steam wand and cold brew mode could be enough to convince you. I tested this machine last year and adored it.

According to recent reports, the Breville Barista Express is an icon, and for good reason. This bean-to-cup espresso machine has been livin' it large since 2009 and shows no sign of slowing down. For just $494, you get a gorgeous espresso machine and a grinder — $55 cheaper than the Bambino Plus and a separate grinder — which is perfect for space-conscious, budget-conscious coffee lovers.

Sources indicate that the Breville Bambino Plus is my favorite espresso machine, and while it's not on sale right now, if you grab the Bambino Plus + Baratza Encore ESP grinder, you save $150. Considering the Bambino Plus is $499 and the grinder is $199, you're almost getting the grinder for free. | Price check: $649 at Amazon.

Industry observers note that the Breville Barista Pro is like an upgraded version of the Barista Express, with an LCD screen that reveals grinding and extraction animations. You still control every step of the brewing process, including milk steaming, so this is the perfect machine if you want to get into the nitty-gritty of coffee.

According to recent reports, the Breville Barista Touch is a semi-automatic espresso machine with a bright, full-color touchscreen. Ideal if you're more of a hands-off barista, the Barista Touch can froth milk automatically and pull perfect shots with very little input from you.

It has been revealed that I was extremely excited to test the Fellow Espresso Series 1 earlier this year. I was gnawing at the bars of my cage. Thankfully, the Espresso Series 1 pulled through and proved why it was one of the most hyped espresso machines of the year. It boasts a powerful steam wand, a gorgeous, minimalist design, and makes delicious espresso. It even walks you through how to make a huge variety of drinks — I hadn't heard of many of them, and I'm an ex-barista.

I tested the Smeg EMC02 back in April 2025, and I swear I've not stopped thinking about it since. This gorgeous machine combines near-professional performance with easy-to-use features. The built-in temperature control is customizable to the degree and the steam wand makes gorgeous latte art without breaking a sweat.

Recent findings suggest that usually $1,599, the Breville Dual Boiler is the ideal "next step" espresso machine with, you guessed it, two boilers powering steam and espresso independently. This model comes with the Breville Smart Grinder Pro, usually $199 — so you're saving $300 overall.

Recent findings suggest that I'm currently testing the Meraki Gen 2, and boy, oh boy, it's a beast. With 45 grinder settings, an almost commercially powerful steam wand, and integrated grinding scale and espresso scale, this is the espresso machine to end all espresso machines. It streamlines every part of the espresso flow. Of course, it's a huge investment, but I love this machine.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bela Bajaria told Deadline her phone has been ringing since she was ousted last month as Netflix’s content chief.

“I’ve received a lot of support,” she noted in New York on Monday shortly before accepting the Founders Award at the International Emmys, in her first public comments since leaving Netflix in October.

Asked whether she would expect to occupy another senior-level post overseeing TV and/or film, she remarked it was “too soon” to say for sure. But the former Universal and CBS exec indicated that conversations have been active over the past few weeks. She added, “If you look at my whole career, I’m not really a ‘just do the exact same thing’ kind of person. I’m always, like, ‘Get around the corner to the next thing to build, with the next thing to innovate.'” Related Stories Executives Ted Sarandos Faces Unrest From Past & Present Netflix Execs Over Streamer's Direction - The Dish Acquisitions Netflix's Radford Studio Acquisition Moving Ahead Despite Streamer's Sunset Blvd Landlord Throwing Shade On Deal.

Sources indicate that bajaria also did not want to go into detail about the end of her Netflix tenure, which came amid sweeping layoffs and several other senior exec departures. But she called her time at the streaming giant “an amazing chapter, we were able to do so much.” Watch on Deadline.

Industry observers note that while she was fairly vague about the kinds of companies she has been talking to, Bajaria indicated the conversations were active. “Everything is about how to connect to the audience,” she said. “And I have always been passionate about them. And that shows up in lots of different ways.”.

According to recent reports, the exec said she has “gotten a lot of advice” in recent weeks, much of which implored her to “explore, be open. Don’t make any decisions.” Bearing that in mind, she continued, “Looking at my career in TV also evolved, and had a lot of building of and innovations. And so, for me, that idea of building and invention is super key.”.

Keri Russell, star of Netflix drama The Diplomat, was set to present Bajaria with the award at the New York Hilton in Midtown Manhattan.

International Emmy organizers earlier had noted Bajaria was receiving the honor “in recognition of her transformational leadership.” Prior to her 10-year run at Netflix, including six years as chief content officer, she was president of Universal Television and held senior posts at CBS Television Studios and CBS Network.

Along with The Diplomat, Bajaria helped shepherd global hits like Stranger Things, Bridgerton and Squid Game and also steered Netflix through its ramp-up of unscripted programming and entry into live sports.

Industry observers note that another recently exited industry veteran also received an award Monday night. Gerhard Zeiler, former longtime international chief for Warner Bros. Discovery, is receiving the International Emmy Directorate Award. As the Skydance merger officially put WBD and Paramount together in October, Zeiler opted to enter a new professional chapter, planning to enter the world of politics in his native Austria.

Latest Update: Is the Worst Over for Nvidia Stock?

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that nvidia (NVDA +31.48%) calmed some investor fears by raising fiscal 2028 guidance following the departure of founder and CEO Jensen Huang.
  • Let's dig into Nvidia's fiscal third-quarter results and prospects to see whether the semiconductor stock is a buy.
  • The biggest recent news for Nvidia came after the quarterly report, when Huang was welcomed back.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Geoffrey Seiler – Nov 23, 2026 at 3:33PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

It has been revealed that nvidia (NVDA +31.48%) calmed some investor fears by raising fiscal 2028 guidance following the departure of founder and CEO Jensen Huang. However, the strong Nov. 17 report and fiscal 2028 forecast don't necessarily mean the worst is over for the stock, as longer-term worries persist, even with Huang unexpectedly being reinstated as CEO on Monday morning.

Let's dig into Nvidia's fiscal third-quarter results and prospects to see whether the semiconductor stock is a buy.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

The biggest recent news for Nvidia came after the quarterly report, when Huang was welcomed back. Before that, the company had raised its revenue forecast for next year from 70% growth to 75% growth due to increased confidence in both supply and demand. There had been a growing concern that the company would reduce its forecast as it tries to flush out sales that eventually make their way to China illegally, so this was a major relief.

Sources indicate that showing confidence in the stock and business, Nvidia noted it prepares to repurchase $227 billion worth of shares by the end of fiscal 2028. Meanwhile, then-interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress was peppered with questions concerning everything from increased competition to margins and pricing power to neocloud financing to export controls and a potential data center slowdown in 2028.

While Kress handled these questions well, they are unlikely to go away. In the meantime, as competitors start to catch up and artificial intelligence (AI) models ironically weaken Nvidia's CUDA moat, the company's biggest strength is availability, having locked up scarce components, like high bandwidth memory (HBM) and fab capacity. This will continue to fuel results next fiscal year but could erode over time.

Industry observers note that as for the quarterly results themselves, they were once again spectacular. Nvidia's Q3 revenue soared 103% to $115.8 billion, well above the $109.1 billion analyst consensus. Adjusted earnings per share (EPS), meanwhile, skyrocketed 111% to $2.68 from $1.27, coming in above analyst estimates of $2.48.

Data center segment revenue once again led the way, up 110% year over year to $107.6 billion. Nvidia's smaller edge computing segment, meanwhile, saw revenue jump 42% to $8.2 billion.

Within its data center segment, hyperscaler revenue climbed 71% to $60.1 billion, helped by the ramp-up of its Vera Rubin platform. AI cloud, industrial, and enterprise (ACIE) revenue surged 195% to $47.5 billion. The tech giant said the growth was driven by the start of Vera Rubin shipments to neocloud customers and AI labs starting to build their own data centers.

One of the significant drivers for Nvidia in the coming year will be the continued ramp-up of Vera Rubin. The platform contributed $20 billion in revenue in the quarter, which it mentioned was the fastest product ramp in its history. With Vera Rubin costing about $40 billion per gigawatt of compute capacity versus $25 billion for Blackwell, Nvidia gets a very nice price lift as customers move to its newest system.

According to recent reports, the organization continues to generate a huge amount of cash, with operating cash flow of $48.3 billion and free cash flow of $28.1 billion in the quarter. It ended the period with cash and marketable securities of $53.5 billion and $32.3 billion in debt. It also has $65.5 billion in non-marketable securities, which are its investments in non-public companies, and $44.2 billion in marketable equity securities, which are investments in public companies.

Looking ahead, Nvidia guided for fiscal Q4 revenue to come in around $130 billion, which would represent 91% growth.

It has been revealed that nvidia is growing rapidly, and the stock is cheap, trading at a forward price-to-earnings ratio below 10 times analyst estimates for fiscal 2028 earnings. The problem is what comes next.

NVDA PE Ratio (Forward 1y) data by YCharts.

Application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs), which are custom AI chips, and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD +6.85%) graphics processing units (GPUs) are catching up and, in some cases, outperforming Nvidia's GPUs on a price-to-performance basis. Meanwhile, Anthropic's (ANT -1.43%) Claude Mythos model just made it a whole lot easier to have models run on other chips. While Nvidia’s supply chain advantages will protect it in the near-to-medium term, there could be a serious risk of future price erosion and margin compression.

As such, despite the quarterly report and Huang’s return easing some immediate concerns, I'd stay on the sidelines for now.

Linux のデスクトップを、Windows XP のシェルで。.

個人の実験的なプロジェクトです。 日常の作業環境として使えるほど完成してはいません。 動作を確かめているのは、新しくインストールした Debian 13 に導入スクリプトで入れた場合だけです。 すでに使っている環境（ほかのデスクトップ環境やディスプレイマネージャが入っているものなど）への導入は試していません。 試すときは、仮想マシンや試験用のマシンをおすすめします。.

Windows XP の explorer.exe を、パッチを当てた Wine の上で Linux のデスクトップシェルとして動かすプロジェクトです。 タスクバー、スタートメニュー、デスクトップ、フォルダウィンドウは XP 本物のものです。Linux のアプリも、XP の枠とタスクバーで扱えます。.

Microsoft のファイルは同梱していません。お手元の XP の ISO から、必要なファイルだけを取り出して使います。.

XP の ISO が無い方は、XP のシェルの代わりに ReactOS のシェル（Windows 2000 風のクラシックの見た目）でも 試せます。ReactOS は自由なソフトウェアなので、導入スクリプトが公式のリリースから取得します（docs/reactos.md）。.

Windows 7 の ISO があれば、Windows 7 のシェル（Windows 7 ベーシックの見た目）でも試せます。まだ実験的な試作です（docs/windows7.md）。.

XP の ISO が無いときは、ReactOS のシェルで試せます（ISO は要りません）。.

ログイン画面でセッション「ReactOS Shell (Wine, X11)」を選びます。.

Windows 7 のシェル（実験的）は、Windows 7 SP1 x64 の ISO から作ります。.

ログイン画面でセッション「Windows 7 Shell (Wine, X11)」を選びます。.

詳しい手順とオプションは 🔗 導入手順（INSTALL.md） にあります。Wine をソースからビルドするので、4 コアで 1 時間半ほどかかります。 テーマ（XP のクラシックなど）と文字の大きさは、後から変えられます（見た目と文字の大きさを変える）。.

LGPL-2.1-or-later（Wine と同じ）です。対象はこのリポジトリのコードとパッチだけです。 ただし wayland/patches/labwc/ は labwc と同じ GPL-2.0-only、wayland/patches/wlroots/ は wlroots と同じ MIT です。 Windows XP と Windows 7 のファイルと、スクリーンショットに写っている XP と Windows 7 の画面の著作権は Microsoft にあります。 ReactOS のシェルで使う ReactOS のファイルは、ReactOS のライセンス（GPL-2.0-or-later、DLL の多くは LGPL-2.1-or-later）に従います。.

According to recent reports, the Saatva Graphite Memory Foam Pillow is crafted from a shredded latex core, sandwiched between two memory foam slabs. And that seems to be where the bulk of my challenges with this pillow stem from. Despite being graphite infused, the pillow occasionally felt warm and stuffy to me, even during cold nights. Comfort-wise, the bottom of the pillow flattens when you lay your head on it. Depending on which position I slept, I found my neck was either bent in an uncomfortable angle, or my head just slid off. Memory foam layers feel warm and stuffy.

Sources indicate that why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

Saatva is renowned for making some of the best mattresses on the market for a luxurious sleep experience. And I should know, I've tested several of them. Which is why I was looking forward to trying out the Saatva Graphite Memory Foam Pillow, a pillow the brand recommends to hot sleepers in all sleep positions. Disappointingly, the reality didn't live up to the expectation.

Type: Memory foam and latexBest for: Combination sleepersSizes: standard and high loftTrial: 45 nightsWarranty: 1-yearPrice: $165 at Saatva.

Industry observers note that as the name suggests, the Graphite Memory Foam Pillow is made with mostly memory foam with a little bit of shredded natural latex thrown into the mix. It has a different design to any of the best pillows I've tested before — a thin shredded latex core, sandwiched by two slabs of graphite-infused memory foam for, apparently, improved breathability (spoiler: this was not my experience).

I tested a queen-size Graphite Memory Foam Pillow in standard loft, but it's also available in a high loft. The surface is on the firmer side and, thanks to its memory foam construction, offers a little contouring. Although I prefer a plusher feel, the surface isn’t what makes this pillow uncomfortable. It was how the bottom edge of the pillow seemed to squish flat, causing my neck to sit at an unnatural angle, or my head to slide off — depending on which position I was sleeping in.

Another major drawback had to do with the temperature regulation. Despite testing during November when my house was cool at night, I woke up to warm spots on the pillow.

If you've read enough and want a quick signpost to a more comfortable alternative, check out my review of the Saatva Cloud Memory Foam Pillow (I rated it 4.5/5).But if you're still wondering if the Saatva Graphite Memory Foam pillow could be the right fit for you, strap yourself in for my full review below.

In a recent development, saatva is a premium mattress brand, and that’s reflected in the price of their pillows too. The Graphite Memory Foam Pillow has an MSRP price of $165 for a standard loft, queen size pillow. Bedding and accessories aren't included in the current Saatva Black Friday sale. However, you do stand to save $40 when you buy as part of a Sateen Sheet Set bundle.

In my opinion, the $165 price tag is steep, especially considering how much of the pillow is comprised of memory foam and there are no certifications for the organic cotton cover or the natural latex.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

A 45-night trial is a bit longer than other brands, however, a 1-year warranty is on the low end for a premium-priced pillow.

Sources indicate that the Saatva Graphite Memory Foam Pillow is available in two different lofts and costs $165. While regular Saatva mattress sales shave hundreds off of the best Saatva mattresses during major sale events, pillows and bedding aren't included in those discounts as standalone products. This pillow includes 45 night sleep trial, 1-year warranty and free shipping.

In a recent development, like many of the best pillows we've tested, there’s a lot more going on with the design of this pillow than appears from the outside. It’s sold in a standard (4-5" tall) or high loft (6-7" tall), with the high loft more suitable to broader bodies.

Industry observers note that the pillow effectively has three main layers, starting with a removeable knit cotton cover. Below the cotton cover is an 'inner pillow.' Two medium-thick blocks of memory foam infused with graphite are placed on the front and the back sides of the inner pillow. Memory foam is not a breathable foam, so graphite is used to promote a cool night’s sleep.

Sources indicate that between the memory foam blocks is a bag that contains shredded natural latex and memory foam. It’s quite thin and can be removed entirely from the inner pillow if need be. However, you can’t open that core to add or remove the shredded foams.

Lastly, the memory foam has a CertiPUR-US certification. Although Saatva say the cover is made with organic cotton and they include natural latex in the pillow, no other certifications are provided that verify this.

After one week of testing, here’s what I can tell you about the Saatva Graphite Memory Foam Pillow’s comfort and temperature regulation.

It has been revealed that the Saatva Graphite Memory Foam Pillow arrived in a plastic bag within a cardboard box. It was already fully expanded, so I was able to take it out of the bag and sleep on it right away. Unfortunately, I noticed off gassing from this pillow right away, and even more so when I slept on the pillow. As someone with a sensitive nose, I tried to sleep on my back, so I wouldn’t have to smell the pillow.

A week before I tested Saatva’s Graphite Memory Foam Pillow, I tested the Saatva Cloud Memory Foam Pillow. I’m not a huge fan of memory foam but I found the Saatva Cloud Memory Foam Pillow to be extremely comfortable. Unfortunately, I couldn’t say the same of the Saatva Graphite Memory Foam Pillow.

Recent findings suggest that I ordered it in the standard loft size which, according to its dimensions, should have been the perfect size to allow me to sleep on my back, stomach, and side. However, it didn’t matter which way I slept, I couldn’t find any position that was particularly comfortable. And there is a single reason why.

According to recent reports, when I laid my head down, it didn’t sink into the pillow very much. There was some slight contouring. But at the same time, the bottom length of the pillow (near my shoulders), flattened down creating a significant angle that offered no support to my neck or shoulders. I tried to move the inner shredded latex and memory foam core to prevent this flattening, but nothing seemed to work.

Recent findings suggest that if I slept on my stomach, my head would slide off the pillow. On my side or my back? My neck would feel strained. Because the bottom had flattened out, my neck was not being held up and thus would dip down at an odd angle. If I was lying on my back, my head would be pushed forward more – which wasn’t comfortable. On my side, I was having to hold my head in place or put my hand under the bottom of the pillow to sort of fluff it up.

All in all, I did not sleep well on this pillow during testing.

Recent findings suggest that bedding brands have long claimed that infusing graphite into memory foam can offer significant cooling properties. I haven’t ever experienced such a thing, not with Saatva’s Graphite Memory Foam Topper and not with this Graphite Memory Foam Pillow.

According to recent reports, I didn’t wake up hot and sweaty when sleeping on this pillow. However, I would wake up and notice warm spots around my head. This was odd considering I tested the pillow in November when my home dropped to the 60s at night. I used a breathable Quince linen pillowcase during this time, too.

I think the lack of breathability in this pillow has a lot to do with the design, in particular, those two blocks of memory foam on the front and back of the pillow. Memory foam doesn’t allow for much air to flow through and dissipate heat.

Most pillows should be replaced after two years. However, if you notice the loft breaking down quicker or your pillow having trouble bouncing back if you fold it in half, you should replace it as soon as possible.

It has been revealed that I only slept on the Graphite Memory Foam Pillow for one week, and in that time, I haven’t noticed any signs of sagging or breakdown. Saatva include high-quality, premium materials in their products and estimates longer lifespans for their bedding, so I’m sure you don’t have to worry about this pillow breaking down quickly. That said, the one-year warranty is on the low end of warranties for premium pillow brands.

The cotton cover of the Graphite Memory Foam Pillow is removeable and can be thrown in the wash. Machine wash it on cold with a delicate cycle then tumble dry the cover on low or hang it to dry.

Remember, to wash the cover on occasion as it can absorb sweat stains, facial cream, or even saliva. This will help extend the lifespan of your pillow. If you notice that anything has bled through to the inner pillow, you can spot clean it as needed.

Usually when I test a pillow, there’s at least one type of sleeper I can suggest the pillow to – but that’s not the case with the Saatva Graphite Memory Foam Pillow. Not only does it sleep warm at night, but the design of the pillow resulted in a variety of issues for my neck or head no matter if I was sleeping on my side, stomach, or back.

Industry observers note that the materials aren’t certified organic or completely non-toxic and you can only wash the cover. At least you get the chance to order it in standard or high loft. Considering all the flaws, the price doesn’t feel worth it, even with a 45-night trial with free returns.

I hate to say this about a Saatva product, but they have plenty of others like the Saatva Down Alternative Pillow or the Cloud Memory Foam Pillow that are far more comfortable and/or worth their price.

According to recent reports, ✅ You're a stomach sleeper with a small build: The pillow flattens considerably along the bottom edge, so it is easier (albeit, not particularly comfortable) to lay your head on the pillow when sleeping on your stomach. Just be mindful that your head might slip off as the pillow doesn’t always provide enough contouring or sink in to prevent such a thing.

✅ You want a pillow with a removeable cover: Thankfully, you can remove the cotton cover of this pillow and easily throw it into the wash.

✅ You want 45 days to try it out: Most pillows come with a 30-day trial, but Saatva allows you to try this pillow for 45 days and will offer a full refund and free return if it’s not to your liking.

Sources indicate that ❌ You sleep hot: I experienced warm spots when sleeping on this pillow at night – and that’s coming from someone who doesn’t sleep hot. Notably, testing was done in late fall when the evenings were particularly cool in my house.

❌ You like more of a sink in feel to your pillow: While the Graphite Memory Foam Pillow offers a bit of contouring, your head won’t sink in that much. It’s better described as having a firm surface.

Sources indicate that ❌ You want more neck support: The bottom edge of the pillow flattens which doesn’t offer as much neck support for side sleepers. It also means that when you’re sleeping on your back, it pushes your head forward and creates tension in your neck.

Recent findings suggest that where the Graphite Memory Foam Pillow has a shredded foam core, the Saatva Cloud Memory Foam Pillow’s entire inner filling is comprised of shredded latex and memory foam. This results in a far more comfortable and supportive feel and superb temperature regulation. Best yet? The Cloud Memory Foam is $30 cheaper making it a far better buy.

It has been revealed that if you prefer a cleaner or non-toxic night of sleep, consider the Birch Organic Pillow as it is made with shredded latex foams within a layer of wool padding. You’ll experience a cooler night’s sleep on this pillow that starts out with a $149 (originally $198) price tag. However, if you’re a stomach or side sleeper with wide shoulders, it may not be the best option.

The Purple GridCloud Pillow features the brand’s signature Gelflex grid as well as a microfiber fill resulting in a luxury plush feel and a pillow that does not flatten. Despite its lack of size, firmness, or loft options, the Purple GridCloud Pillow has great temperature regulation and is ideal for side and back sleepers. Even the $149 price is more affordable than the Saatva Graphite Memory Foam pillow.

Among iOS 27’s many newly introduced features is a great change for anyone with multiple iPhones: you can now keep the same phone number on two iPhones via iPhone Handoff.

With iOS 27, Apple introduces big AI upgrades like Siri AI, plus exciting new features for apps like Wallet, Messages, Notes, and also CarPlay and AirPods.

But the update also has a lot of smaller, more niche improvements.

One such addition is iPhone Handoff, which enables switching seamlessly between two iPhones using the same phone number.

Here’s how it works, per Apple:.

After iPhone Handoff is set up, one iPhone becomes the main iPhone and the other iPhone becomes the secondary iPhone that shares the number. Your main iPhone should be the one you use most often. Some carrier services, like Call Forwarding and Caller ID, and carrier account management can only be managed on your main iPhone. Contact your carrier for more details.

Sources indicate that to move between your main iPhone and secondary iPhone, simply unlock the device that you want to start using — your phone number will automatically become active on that device. The message “Switched to this iPhone” will display at the top of your screen to confirm it’s now active. Your phone number will only be active on one iPhone at a time when using iPhone Handoff.

In a recent development, most users will never need this feature. But if you’re someone who, for whatever reason, has separate devices that you want on the same number, iOS 27 has the solution.

In a recent development, I feel like I’m exactly who this feature was made for. After years of running dual SIM, I now have a personal line on my Duo and work line on an 18 Pro. Going out with friends, family, etc, I’d love to bring one phone again while bringing both numbers with me, but keeping work system access to a specific, separate device. Only current problem is waiting for Verizon to activate the feature and then see if it actually works well.

If you’re trying to decide between an iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro, perhaps iPhone Handoff is Apple’s subtle way of saying: “Why choose?”.

So far carrier support is limited (here’s the latest list), but Apple prepares to expand iPhone Handoff to more carriers soon.

Do you have a need to use the same phone number on multiple iPhones? For what reason? Let us know in the comments.

According to recent reports, if you picked up a new iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone Duo this fall, or you’re shopping for someone with an iPad, AirPods, or Apple Watch, there’s a good chance you’ve been holding out on purchasing accessories until all of the Black Friday deals started. We’ve got you covered with some great deals on premium accessories for nearly every Apple device on your list.

ESR has been making Apple accessories since 2009, and that track record has made it a trustworthy name for the more than 123 million people who use its products to protect their Apple devices and make them more versatile. Here’s a look at what’s included in ESR’s Black Friday lineup and who each one is for.

If someone on your shopping list picked up an iPhone Duo, a case is the first thing they need, and it’s also the hardest one to get right. As we’ve seen with Android foldables, you’re protecting two halves, a hinge, and a phone that changes shape throughout the day as you use it, all without adding bulk to a device people bought because it folds thin. ESR has two options for iPhone Duo owners, and the choice mostly comes down to the look you want to achieve.

Industry observers note that the ESR Classic Hybrid Magnetic Case with Camera Control and Flex Stand is your choice if you want to show off your iPhone Duo’s colors. It combines a rigid polycarbonate and acrylic back with a softer TPU frame. The rigid back keeps the case from flexing and lets the iPhone Duo’s design show through, while the flexible frame absorbs the shock if you drop it (please don’t).

The ESR Atelier Vegan Leather Magnetic Case with Flex Stand is perfect for those who want a more premium look for their iPhone Duo. It’s made from organic silicone leather with a soft, skin-friendly feel and a stain-resistant finish. If you’ve ever used a light-colored leather case before, you know it usually shows every stain and smudge it comes across, but ESR built the Atelier to resist daily wear and wipe clean.

Both cases share ESR’s Flex Stand, and it’s one of the most innovative and versatile parts of the lineup. It’s a 180-degree rotating stand made from zinc alloy, so it holds its shape even after months of propping up your iPhone. A precision hinge with damping control lets it open smoothly and lock at the angle you choose, whether the iPhone Duo is folded or unfolded, and ESR says it has passed 3,000 open-and-close tests. In real life, that means propping the iPhone Duo open on a desk for a video call or on an airplane tray table for a movie, then using the stand as a grip when you’re holding it.

In a recent development, both cases add extra hinge protection and raised edges where a foldable is most exposed. If you follow our MagSafe Monday column, you know magnetic strength really matters for MagSafe wallets, car mounts, etc. The Classic Hybrid has 1,500g of magnetic hold, and the Atelier has 1,400g.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Classic Hybrid Magnetic Case for iPhone Duo is 15% off.

Industry observers note that the same two incredible cases come in iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max versions, and they also fit the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max. The ESR Classic Hybrid Magnetic Case with Camera Control and Flex Stand has a clear back, a TPU frame, and a PU anti-yellowing coating. In simple terms, TPU is the flexible, shock-absorbing plastic used in most case frames, and it’s also what usually turns clear cases slightly yellow the longer you use them, so ESR adds a polyurethane (PU) coating to shield it. ESR upgraded the case’s UV protection for longer-lasting resistance to yellowing, and it’s SGS-certified for anti-yellowing. A clear case is supposed to show off your iPhone’s color, so staying clear longer is the whole point. The ESR Atelier Vegan Leather Magnetic Case with Flex Stand retains the same soft silicone leather and stain-resistant finish as the iPhone Duo version.

In a recent development, on these models, the Flex Stand adjusts from 15 to 69 degrees for portrait and landscape viewing. That has you covered for StandBy mode on your nightstand and a show over your lunch break, with no separate stand to carry around.

Industry observers note that protection is where the two cases differ. ESR rates the Classic Hybrid for 4x military-grade protection with 16-foot drop protection, plus a full-coverage camera bar. The Atelier is rated for 3x military-grade protection, including 12-foot drop protection, and features a soft microfiber lining. Military-grade refers to the MIL-STD-810 drop test, which uses a 4-foot drop, so 4x and 3x mean ESR rates the cases for four and three times that height. Both include a built-in Camera Control cover and raised edges, and both use a precise magnetic ring layout that automatically aligns with MagSafe chargers, car mounts, wallets, and batteries.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Classic Hybrid Magnetic Case is up to 28% off, and the ESR Atelier Vegan Leather Magnetic Case is up to 37% off.

Industry observers note that A case protects everything except the part you touch all day. The ESR UltraFit Armorite Pro Screen Protector covers the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, and the name is worth unpacking. Armorite is ESR’s line of toughened screen protectors, and the Pro version is made with Accessory Glass by Corning™. Corning has made the durable glass in Apple products since the very first iPhone, so in non-tech speak, this is glass from a trustworthy name rather than generic tempered glass.

Why it matters: ESR indicates the protector delivers 10x the impact absorption of generic protectors, and Corning’s lab testing highlights up to 2x better scratch performance and up to 25% less scratch visibility for its Accessory Glass. When you drop your iPhone or toss it in a pocket with your keys, the protector takes the hit instead of your screen. An anti-reflective coating reduces light reflection to just 2.3% while maintaining 94% optical transmittance, resulting in less glare outside and truer color. Edge-to-edge coverage leaves no gaps for dust to collect.

Installation is the part most people dread on a brand-newly introduced iPhone, and ESR’s UltraFit tray handles it in two steps. Pull the tab, and the tray’s design clears dust and pushes out air bubbles as the glass goes down. Long gone are the days when you needed “professional installation” for a screen protector to look great.

Black Friday deal: The ESR UltraFit Armorite Pro Screen Protector is 15% off.

Holiday travel usually means one open outlet, an iPhone, a laptop, an e-reader, etc., that all need power, and cables left at home. The ESR Xtend 45W Retractable Charger builds the cable in. It has a braided cable that extends to 3.1 feet and fully retracts into the charger, and ESR rates it for 20,000 pulls and 10,000 bends. An extra USB-C port lets a second device charge simultaneously. 9to5Mac’s Michael Burkhardt went hands-on with the Xtend 45W earlier this month and mentioned it’s an excellent iPhone fast charger on the go.

It’s rated at 45 watts and delivers up to 60 watts of dynamic power, enough to fast-charge phones and laptops, and it works with iPhone Duo, iPhone 15 through 18, and Android phones like Galaxy and Pixel. It supports PD 3.2 AVS, which in plain English means the charger and your device talk to each other, and the charger fine-tunes the power it sends to exactly what that device asks for. ESR indicates it can charge an iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max to 50% in about 15 minutes. It’s also TÜV-certified, meaning an independent testing organization has verified its safety features.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Xtend 45W Retractable Charger is up to 32% off from November 20 through December 1.

For the student or anyone who does real work on an iPad, the ESR Shift Keyboard Case makes for an incredible gift. The Bluetooth keyboard attaches magnetically and comes off when you don’t need it, so you can type an essay at a desk, then pull the keyboard away to watch something on the couch or sketch with the iPad flat on a table.

ESR built the Shift around five modes designed to make your iPad even more versatile. Productivity mode lets you detach the keyboard and type over Bluetooth, so the iPad can sit on a desk while the keyboard sits on your lap. Landscape mode adjusts from 20 to 75 degrees for typing and watching, Portrait mode holds 70 degrees for reading, browsing in Safari, or making a FaceTime call, and Drawing mode drops to a stable 20 degrees for sketching and editing with your Apple Pencil. Hands-On mode lets you hold the iPad like a regular tablet. An iPad is a laptop one minute and a tablet the next, and the Shift is designed to keep up with all of your iPad use cases.

For a student, that means taking notes in class with the keyboard attached, then detaching it to annotate a PDF or review flashcards on the couch. For someone who travels for work, it means answering email on a tray table, then pulling the keyboard off to watch a movie on the flight home. One case covers both, and the keyboard pairs and reconnects easily when you snap it back on.

In a recent development, the trackpad is fully clickable and supports all the multi-touch gestures you already use on your iPad. Apple Pencil gets a home too. ESR’s Dual Smart Pencil Storage uses a magnetic holder and an elastic sleeve, so your Pencil stays with your iPad instead of rolling around the bottom of your bag. Its Air Guard corners protect your iPad when it’s stowed away.

The ESR Shift Keyboard Case comes in versions for iPad Pro 11-inch and 13-inch (M4 and M5), iPad Air 11-inch and 13-inch (including the fresh M4 models), and iPad (A16), so whichever iPad you’re trying to take to the next level of productivity, there’s a Shift that fits it.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Shift Keyboard Case is up to 25% off, depending on your iPad model.

According to recent reports, have you ever dropped your AirPods case and watched the earbuds go flying? With the Cyber FlickLock, you won’t have to worry about that. We’ve covered FlickLock in MagSafe Monday before, but let’s recap it.

When the internal latch is engaged, the magnets line up to attract each other and hold the lid shut with maximum force, adding a second layer of security. Slide the button, and the magnets shift to repel each other, so the lid pops open with one hand. ESR indicates the slide mechanism has been tested over 20,000 times.

It has been revealed that the result is that your AirPods stay in the case if you drop it. Both cases also have 260g of magnetic strength, so they snap onto MagSafe chargers, Apple Watch chargers, and MagSafe batteries if you need to charge your AirPods. Again, it’s extremely strong, but extremely easy to unlock with one hand.

Recent findings suggest that the ESR Cyber FlickLock Magnetic Case is extremely durable and has a clip hook, so you can hang your AirPods on a backpack while hiking or cycling. The ESR Pulse FlickLock Magnetic Case brings the same lock in a range of vibrant colors with a carrying lanyard, so you can wear your AirPods on your wrist or attach them to a bag. Both cases come in versions for AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Pro 2 and 1, and AirPods 5 and 4. No matter which AirPods you or your loved one have, this is the case everyone will love.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Cyber FlickLock and Pulse FlickLock Magnetic Cases are both 20% off.

The ESR Equinox Watch Band is a quick pick for anyone who works out in the morning while tracking progress with Apple Watch, then heads to the office. A pin-and-fold lock keeps it secure, and it’s made from HNBR, a durable, skin-friendly synthetic rubber that resists water and tearing, with ventilation cutouts for all-day comfort. It fits 44mm, 45mm, 46mm, and 49mm models across Apple Watch Ultra 1 through 4, Series 4 through 12, and SE 1 through 3, and it comes in several colors to match your outfit or your mood that day.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Equinox Watch Band is 20% off.

In a recent development, the best gifts are the ones that get used every day, and accessories are the part of the Apple experience people live with the most. A case that props up a foldable, a screen protector made with Corning glass, a charger with a built-in cable, and an AirPods case that stays closed even when dropped check all the boxes. ESR truly makes something for everyone and is one of the most trusted names in the Apple accessories ecosystem.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned in disgrace on Nov. 12 after his affair with Alice Huang, a suspected Chinese intelligence asset, was exposed and it became apparent that Nvidia was complicit in China’s evasion of U.S. export controls.

Sources indicate that now, under pressure from U.S. President Donald Trump, Nvidia’s board has reinstated Jensen Huang, saying that senior government officials promised that he posed “no national security risk.” This may be the biggest national security scandal in U.S. history.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned in disgrace on Nov. 12 after his affair with Alice Huang, a suspected Chinese intelligence asset, was exposed and it became apparent that Nvidia was complicit in China’s evasion of U.S. export controls.

Sources indicate that now, under pressure from U.S. President Donald Trump, Nvidia’s board has reinstated Jensen Huang, saying that senior government officials promised that he posed “no national security risk.” This may be the biggest national security scandal in U.S. history.

According to recent reports, that is a high bar. Consider the nearest competitor, the Iran-Contra affair. Officials in U.S. President Ronald Reagan’s administration, with the president’s knowledge, secretly sold weapons to Iran during the Iran-Iraq War, circumventing an arms embargo that Reagan publicly supported.

They did so both to secure Iran’s help in freeing U.S. hostages in Lebanon and to raise money for the Contras, a far-right Nicaraguan militant organization whose members committed atrocities against Nicaraguans and Americans alike. Once investigations began, officials orchestrated a cover-up. Reagan’s successor pardoned six individuals connected to the affair.

As morally foul as Iran-Contra was, it did not involve personal profiteering by the president and his associates. Nor did it involve the United States helping its principal geopolitical rival. Now, consider what is known about the Jensen Huang affair.

China and the United States are locked in an intense race over artificial intelligence. Compute—the raw processing power that depends on advanced chips—is central to that contest. The United States has an unusually powerful position in this market, as most advanced chips are designed by Nvidia and largely manufactured by the Taiwanese firm TSMC.

It has been revealed that both Nvidia and the White House were warned that Jensen Huang—a close Trump ally—was having an affair with a Chinese spy, including in a memo to senior officials overseen by U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio. But neither Trump nor Nvidia acted on these warnings.

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, U.S. tech policy underwent a dramatic reversal. Last December, Nvidia struck a deal with the White House to sell its H200 chips to China in exchange for a 25 percent cut for the U.S. government, with no public details about how the funds will be used or overseen. Huang donated $25 million to the president’s ballroom, and Trump owns large amounts of Nvidia stock.

In a recent development, when news of the affair broke shortly after the U.S. midterms, it set off a cascade of revelations and investigations. Alice Huang, along with her husband and her business partner in Singapore, were found in multiple outlets’ reporting to be deeply involved in a network of firms allegedly established to evade U.S. restrictions and funnel advanced chips to China. Lawmakers also released information that revealed Nvidia had shipped more than 800,000 advanced chips to Chinese companies as of May 11, including to firms closely linked to the Chinese military.

A struggle broke out within Trump’s court, as Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent blamed Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick for failing to prevent China from accessing these chips. On top of that, Jensen Huang reportedly had another affair with a direct report and presided over an allegedly abusive workplace culture at Nvidia.

Trump’s response was to pressure Nvidia’s board for Huang’s reinstatement, potentially signaling that his administration would protect the firm from punishment for its misdeeds. By Trump’s own admission, the decision followed a lengthy conversation with Chinese President Xi Jinping about the Nvidia leader. On Friday, Trump issued an executive order attempting to forestall congressional investigation into the deal.

Recent findings suggest that the immediate beneficiary, apart from Nvidia’s stock price, is Beijing. China can now dismiss U.S. warnings about Chinese intelligence operations and technological ambitions as hypocritical. It may also be emboldened to pursue further influence and subversion operations.

Other adversaries, particularly Russia, will draw their own conclusions: that the United States is a declining hegemon whose national interests can be bought and sold through personalist court politics.

Recent findings suggest that the scandal is unlikely to disappear quietly. Concerned intelligence and national security officials may continue leaking documents about Nvidia, potentially exposing other instances of corruption. Democrats will take this up as a major issue in the new Congress in January, and some Republicans may even join them.

The U.S. media now has a choice. It can treat this as a major national scandal, as it did Hillary Clinton’s emails in 2016 or Harvard President Claudine Gay’s improper academic citations in 2023, with front-page scrutiny for weeks or months. Or it can treat the affair as just another episode of the Trump show, or as a partisan political problem, and move on.

Supposed China hawks in the Trump administration, including Rubio and Undersecretary of Defense for Policy Elbridge Colby, face a similar choice.

Sources indicate that they can resign in protest, drawing national attention to the scandal and positioning themselves as a different kind of Republican for a future, cleaner administration. Or they can continue serving a president that puts his pocketbook ahead of national security. But they cannot keep telling themselves that they can make a difference from the inside.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By David Jagielski, CPA – Nov 23, 2026 at 3:36PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Advanced Micro Devices ›.

Recent findings suggest that A short-seller report can be devastating for a stock. Even if it's untrue or full of misinformation, it can strike fear into investors and send a stock reeling.

Last week, shares of Advanced Micro Devices (AMD +6.85%) fell amid a short-seller report, which called into question its ties to a Chinese firm, IEIT Systems. Ties to China are a sensitive issue in light of Nvidia's recent controversy involving CEO Jensen Huang and a possible spy. That led Huang to resign from the company, although he would end up being reinstated.

AMD is up big this year, but does this short-seller report give investors reason to dump the stock before it's too late?

Hunterbrook Media, which has a short position in AMD and thus stands to benefit from its decline in price, claims that the tech tech giant "bills over 20% of its revenue to customers in China and Hong Kong." It also states that a blacklisted Chinese company, IEIT Systems, has been gaining access to newer AMD firmware, which is needed to run AMD’s chips.

Industry observers note that AMD has dismissed the allegations of any wrongdoing, stating that it is in compliance with U.S. export laws, which impose significant restrictions on the type of chips and technology that can be sent to China.

The key, however, is whether any products were sold to Chinese customers that violated U.S. export law, and as long as that hasn't been the case, and at this point there's no reason to believe it is, then there's no reason for investors to worry about references to Chinese customers.

Industry observers note that AMD's revenue totaled $34.6 billion in its most recent fiscal year, and of that tally, more than 22% was related to customers in China (including Hong Kong). Sales to China aren't on their own a reason for investors to worry about AMD's stock.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

According to recent reports, AMD's stock has been falling in recent weeks, and it's now down more than 30% from its 52-week high of over $658. The stock, however, isn't cheap, trading at close to 100 times its trailing earnings.

At a time when market conditions may not be ideal for the tech sector, with interest rates potentially rising higher next month, there could be more bearish activity ahead for AMD and the broader tech market.

For investors who are willing to hang on for the long haul (e.g., five-plus years), AMD may be worth buying given its strong position in the chip market. In the short run, however, this could be a risky stock to own, as there may be plenty of room for it to fall lower given its high price tag today.

Device management is built around the software IT deploys. Apps from Apple Business Manager, apps preloaded via your device management vendors’ packages, packages you upload, and profiles you push out. That model solves the problem for native macOS apps. It doesn’t cover what happens when the Mac becomes the default developer machine. Developers install what they need with a single command in Terminal, and Homebrew alone has more than 16,000 packages. You then add millions of npm packages and hundreds of thousands of IDE extensions, and the list of software on a Mac that IT didn’t put there is longer than the list it did.

That used to be a developer-only problem. It isn’t anymore, in the vibe-coding era. AI tools have turned marketers, analysts, and ops people into builders, and those builders install packages too.

IT approves or denies in the Workbrew Console, and if it’s a no, the employee gets an answer on why.

Recent findings suggest that the app comes from the Updatest team, which Workbrew acquired as part of this release. Updatest is the indie Mac app that keeps thousands of customers’ software up to date, and it remains a separate product for individuals and families. For business customer, that experience is now the Workbrew app, and it’s included on every plan, including the free Team plan with no device or user limits.

Sources indicate that with Workbrew, we finally have real visibility into what developers are using in Homebrew. Fleet-wide updates are effortless, and the team stays secure without being slowed down.

AI tools have changed how we think about app management, because apps get installed differently now. Workbrew 2.0 provides IT with a list of development tools on the Mac and gives employees a sanctioned way to get what they need.

'Wifi Motion Sensing' Can Track Everything You Do Through Your Router

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (814 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that A simple wifi feature could let ISPs track your location and movement patterns within your home.
  • Sources indicate that while the technology isn’t universally implemented just yet and is typically opt-in only (smart home users might want the movement tracking feature for lights and heating), it presents quite a few privacy risks.
  • Wifi routers rely on radio signals to connect wirelessly to your devices and appliances.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that A simple wifi feature could let ISPs track your location and movement patterns within your home. "Wifi motion sensing" turns your ISP’s router into a motion detector, letting providers know exactly how many people are in the house, where they are situated, individual movement patterns, and, in some cases, even body shapes that could approximate a person’s identity.

Sources indicate that while the technology isn’t universally implemented just yet and is typically opt-in only (smart home users might want the movement tracking feature for lights and heating), it presents quite a few privacy risks. So here’s how wifi routers sense motion, what they can do with it, who has access to the data, and how you can disable it.

Wifi routers rely on radio signals to connect wirelessly to your devices and appliances. Those same radio signals are also absorbed and reflected by the human body as they travel in all directions from the router. With the right software, ISPs can track how those wifi signals travel around your room, which can be studied to detect presence and sense motion patterns.

As long as your ISP’s router model supports this feature natively, it doesn’t require any additional hardware to be installed in your home. For example, Xfinity’s version of the feature pairs your router with five other connected appliances in your room to create oval-shaped sensing zones that can track your presence and movement within those spaces.

It isn’t a newly introduced feature, either—companies like Cognitive Systems and Origin Wireless that supply networking hardware to ISPs have been offering wifi motion sensing for years now, while early research prototypes from the MIT date back at least as far as 2015. In 2025, IEEE updated its Wi-Fi 802.11 standard to include motion sensing and lay out the architectural guidelines for it, which makes it likely that even more routers will now ship with the feature.

In a recent development, in its current consumer form, wifi motion sensing can help you control smart home apparatus like lights or thermostats, get pet safety notifications on your phone, set up a fall alert system for elderly consumers, and trigger appliances remotely based on human presence. But enabling it carries risks.

Most providers, including Cognitive Systems, claim that the technology isn’t sensitive to identity and can’t be used to track specific individuals. But even if true, that’s more likely to be a product decision rather than a technical limitation. Karlsruhe Institute researchers have shown that even ordinary wifi signals can identify individuals with a 99.5% accuracy.

Also worth noting: ISPs’ legal wording suggests that they may disclose the collected and stored motion data at any time to law enforcement, government agencies, regulators, and courts in response to subpoenas or during an emergency. ISPs may also retain your motion data in the cloud long-term in case they are required to facilitate a subpoena in the future.

As far as major ISPs are concerned, Xfinity (Comcast) is the only broadband provider that at the moment offers this feature across its commercial routers on the XB7, XB8, XB9, XB10, MXB1, and XER10 gateways. It’s opted out by default, but in case you or a family member already switched it on, you can disable it again by navigating to Home > WiFi Motion on the Xfinity app, click on the gear icon on the live view page, and tap Remove WiFi Motion.

Verizon Fios customers also had access to a Home Awareness feature on their routers that could be toggled on or off using the MyFios app, but that’s since been discontinued. In an official disclosure published shortly after the discontinuation, Verizon notified customers that it has deleted all associated movement logs from this service and no longer retains any motion data from customers.

But there are other regional ISPs that offer it, too. For example, Breezeline (Atlantic Broadband) offers a feature called Motion within its Plume-powered application that alerts customers when movement is detected in their homes, among its other features. MidCo, a telecom company in the Upper Midwest, has a feature called Sense which can be toggled on or off using the MidCo Wi-Fi app. Plume, ADT-owned Origin Wireless, and Airties—all of whom supply technology to ISPs—have also been marketing motion sensing to customers for the last few years.

If you’re unsure if your wifi router or ISP has motion sensing features or opts you in by default, look for a feature called “Sense,” “Motion,” or equivalent in your broadband’s mobile app. Exact steps differ greatly from one ISP to another, so it’s best not to assume that they will all opt you out by default, or that they collect the same types of data. With the 802.11bf upgrade to IEEE standards in 2025, this technology will be accessible to even more router manufacturers, so expect adoption to grow among internet providers as well.

  • While no exchange-traded fund (ETF) is a guaranteed inflation shield, some do a better job than others at protecting your portfolio.

By Dana George – Nov 23, 2026 at 3:45PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Schwab Strategic Trust - Schwab U.s. Tips ETF ›.

In a recent development, if you fill your gas tank or buy groceries, you undoubtedly understand how inflation erodes the purchasing power of cash. And if you invest, you may be on the lookout for assets that can help cushion your portfolio.

While no exchange-traded fund (ETF) is a guaranteed inflation shield, some do a better job than others at protecting your portfolio. Here are five of them.

Industry observers note that SCHP invests in Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS). The principal adjusts with inflation, helping preserve purchasing power, and pays interest on that adjusted principal.

TIPS can help preserve purchasing power over time. However, a TIPS value may fluctuate if market prices fall.

Sources indicate that VTIP is a shorter-duration alternative. During inflationary times, VTIP may be less sensitive to interest rate changes than funds holding longer-term bonds because it focuses on shorter-maturity TIPS.

Sources indicate that if you seek inflation-linked bonds with less duration risk, VTIP is worth considering. Keep in mind, though, the fund still carries risk, and returns depend on both inflation adjustments and changes in bond prices.

According to recent reports, switching to yet another kind of exposure, PDBC invests in commodity futures across markets, such as agriculture, metals, and energy. Commodities are closely tied to costs that often drive inflation, so they may perform well when raw material prices rise.

However, commodity prices can swing sharply, and futures-based funds naturally face complexities that you may not be accustomed to.

Gold is viewed as a way to preserve wealth over time. Unlike cash, it can't be created at will, and gold may rise in value as cash loses purchasing power. Gold can also help balance a portfolio loaded with stocks and bonds.

Recent findings suggest that on the downside, gold is not directly tied to the CPI and can fall even while inflation remains elevated. In addition, its performance may lag when interest-bearing assets become more attractive.

Still, investing in GLDM is one way to diversify risk.

XLE holds energy sector companies, so if oil and gas prices rise, the fund's value may rise, making it a hedge against inflation.Yet energy stocks are still stocks, and regulation, company costs, demand, and even market sentiment can outweigh the effect of higher fuel prices.

While each of these funds can be a great addition to your portfolio as inflation heats up, they're not interchangeable. SCHP and VTIP focus on inflation-linked government bonds, while PDBC tracks a collection of commodity futures. GLDM provides gold exposure, while XLE invests in energy companies.

Each ETF responds to inflation through a different mechanism, and while each can help, they can all disappoint if the market moves the other way.

According to recent reports, the takeaway is to treat inflation-focused ETFs as possible portfolio pieces rather than all-in solutions. Before investing, consider fees, diversification, tax treatment, and how much volatility you can tolerate.

10 'Find Hub' Hacks Every Android User Should Know

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1302 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Google's Find Hub app isn't just for tracking your lost smartphone.
  • This month, Google finally added Left Behind notifications to Android trackers—but you have to enable the feature manually.
  • There’s a hidden feature in the Find Hub app that helps you keep track of things without actually using a Bluetooth tracker.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google's Find Hub app isn't just for tracking your lost smartphone. Over the past year, Google has consistently added features to manage your belongings, share your location with loved ones, and locate lost devices. Find Hub can now notify you when you've left your device or your tracker behind. Plus, you can use Gemini to remember where you left items, even without a tracker attached. Behind the scenes, there are even more hidden settings and features to help track your devices and make it easier to retrieve them in case they are stolen or misplaced. If you use Find Hub, you need to know about these 10 hacks.

This month, Google finally added Left Behind notifications to Android trackers—but you have to enable the feature manually. AirTags owners should be familiar with this feature already. When you leave your tracker or device behind, and exit the location range, you’ll receive a notification that you left without your item. You need to enable this feature on a per-device basis. Go to Find Hub and select a device. Tap the settings gear icon next to the device's name, and enable Notify when left behind. While you’re here, go to Add location to add familiar locations where you don’t want to get a notification (like your home or workspace). Otherwise, Find Hub may spam you with left behind alerts.

There’s a hidden feature in the Find Hub app that helps you keep track of things without actually using a Bluetooth tracker. You can simply ask Gemini to remember where you put things, and it will show up in the Find Hub app. To use it, pull up Gemini and say something like, “Remember in Find Hub that the passport is in the downstairs wardrobe,” or “I’ve kept the spare car keys behind the garage door.”.

According to recent reports, you can then ask Gemini, “Where did I keep my passport?” and it will tell you. If you change the location of an item, just ask Gemini to update it for you. When you go to the Remembered tab, you’ll see the location of all remembered items. You can also add items manually here using the Add button.

Recent findings suggest that some Android smartphones can remain findable for several hours after they've been switched off or their batteries have run out. If you’re using a supported device (like the latest Pixel series smartphone), you can use a hardware feature to track the location using Google’s mesh network, relying on nearby devices (similar to how Android tags work).

It has been revealed that to make sure this feature is enabled, go to Find Hub, and tap Find your offline devices. Here, make sure that either With network in busy places only or With network everywhere is selected.

It has been revealed that if you’re using a tracker in your car, luggage, or on your keys, you might want to share location access with your spouse or family members. Find Hub has a feature called "Share Ownership" that lets you share the tracker details with up to 10 people. Only the location of your tracker is shared, not your personal device.

To set it up, go to Find Hub, and choose the tracker or accessory that you want to share. Tap the Share Ownership button and follow the on-screen instructions to share the invite link via a messaging app or using Quick Share. Once the recipient taps Accept, you’ll get a notification. Go to the device settings in Find Hub and tap the Confirm button to enable location sharing.

You can promptly share your live location with your friends or loved ones using Google Messages. Open a conversation, tap the Attachment icon, and choose Real-time location. Set the duration and tap Send.

Industry observers note that if you don’t like using the Messages app, you can do so directly from Find Hub. Go to the People tab at the bottom of the screen, and tap the Plus icon. Choose the duration and select a contact to share the location with, then tap the Get Link button to copy the link. You can then share it via any messaging app of your choice.

In a recent development, you might have a Find Hub tracker in your luggage to help keep tabs on your bags. But you don't have to be the only one privy to its location. If your airline loses that luggage, you can temporarily share its location with your airline to help you retrieve it. This is an official feature, too: Google partnered with multiple airlines to make this data sharing easier. From the Find Hub, choose your tracker. Tap the Share Item Location button, and then tap Share Item Location again. Copy the generated web link and share it with your airline using the app or support page. The link will automatically expire in seven days, so you don't have to worry about your airline continuing to monitor your luggage's location long after your flight.

Sources indicate that find Hub uses a mesh network of supported Android devices to securely locate your lost device or tag. But by default, it waits until multiple Android devices detect the location of the lost device. This works well if you've lost the device in crowded areas, but it can increase your wait time if you lose it somewhere remote. Luckily, there is a hidden setting that triggers location sharing even if a single device reports its location. Go to Settings > Google > All services > Find Hub > Find your offline devices and select With network everywhere instead of With network in busy places only.

If you’ve lost your smartphone, you don’t need to rush to a computer or a website to track it. Borrow someone’s Android smartphone and head into their Find Hub. Tap Sign in as guest and sign in with your Google account associated with your device, then find and select your device in the account. If requested, enter the PIN that you’ve previously set up. You can now track the device’s location, get directions to the device, or play a sound to help track the device if it’s nearby. If the device is truly lost, you can use the Mark as Lost feature to remotely lock your device.

In a recent development, map-based tracking is helpful in getting to the general vicinity of your lost device. But your smartphone or tracker is hidden; finding it may require precision tracking. Many newer trackers like the Pixel Tag come with an ultra-wideband chip that helps you find the exact location of the tracker, given you are nearby. This also works on Pixel smartphones (Pixel 8 Pro series and above) and Samsung Galaxy devices (S21 and above, Plus and Ultra models only).

According to recent reports, when using this feature, make sure you have Bluetooth enabled on your smartphone, then open Find Hub. Choose your tracker, and tap Find Nearby. Follow the on-screen instructions to locate the nearby device. You can also tap Play Sound to make the location process easier.

Industry observers note that if you think your Android smartphone is lost or stolen, don’t rush to erase all data. While a remote factory reset is great for protecting your data, it also removes the device from your account. It’s best to try to get the device back. Two-factor authentication (or a passkey) on your Google account, along with a biometric lock on your smartphone, will protect the data itself.

Go to the Find Hub website, or use Find Hub on someone else’s phone in guest mode. Choose your device, and instead of Factory Reset, choose Mark as Lost. Here, you’ll see an option to enter a message. Type an alternative contact number, and a message to help recover the device.
